CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right knee injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
William is a patient who sustained a right knee injury one week ago while at a trampoline park with his wife. He reports hearing a snap and experiencing instant pain upon landing on the trampoline. This was his first time visiting a trampoline park. The injury occurred during recreational activity, not as part of a structured exercise program. Pain is localized to the lateral (outside) aspect of the right knee. He has taken acetaminophen for pain management, which provided minimal relief. He has attempted conservative management with elevation. He denies using ice or heat therapy. He reports a limp and difficulty with certain movements, though he is able to bear weight.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies measured blood pressure checks recently. Reports blood sugars are slightly better. States he checks blood sugar most days when he remembers, approximately four to five times per week. Denies other acute systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Type 2 diabetes mellitus

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily (taking most days when remembers)
Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient does not exercise regularly, describing his regimen as inconsistent. Does not work out at the trampoline park often. Denies participation in structured exercise classes. Reports trying to watch diet but not counting calories or following a specific diet plan. Denies keto diet. Attempting to watch carbohydrate intake. Denies low-salt diet focus. Reports reluctance to visit doctors.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure elevated at approximately 180/80 mmHg.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmur appreciated.
Lungs: Clear bilaterally.
Right knee: Ecchymosis and edema noted along the lateral aspect. Tenderness to palpation on lateral aspect; no tenderness on medial aspect. No effusion noted. Able to bend and straighten knee with pain on movement. Decent range of motion maintained. Gait with slight limp noted. Able to bear weight.

RESULTS
Right knee X-ray: No evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right knee pain - Lateral ligament strain. Start meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain and swelling. Refer to physical therapy for strengthening and injury prevention. Advise follow-up imaging if pain persists. Anticipated self-limited course.
2. Hypertension - Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Order echocardiogram given concern about blood pressure control. Consider medication modification pending results.
3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus - Order HbA1c to assess long-term glycemic control. Order lipid panel to determine if medication adjustments needed.
